**Research Brief: U.S. Department of Labor Tweet on Wages and Prices (March 13, 2026)**  

On March 13, 2026, the U.S. Department of Labor tweeted: “That Friday feeling when wages are going up and prices are coming down for American workers 💸🇺🇸” (https://x.com/i/status/2032514777663021439). The post implies that wages are rising in real terms and that overall prices are declining. However, official data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) and other federal sources show that this characterization is inaccurate: **real average hourly earnings actually fell over the year, and inflation remained positive (prices continued to rise, not fall).**  

**Wages: nominal increases, but real earnings declined**  
According to the BLS’s *Real Earnings Summary* for April 2026 (published May 12, 2026), “From April 2025 to April 2026, real average hourly earnings decreased 0.3 percent, seasonally adjusted” (https://www.bls.gov/news.release/realer.nr0.htm). A parallel DOL news release states a decrease of 0.2 percent (https://www.dol.gov/newsroom/economicdata/realer_05122026.pdf). While nominal average hourly earnings rose 3.6% year-over-year as of April 2026 (Trading Economics, citing BLS data: https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/average-hourly-earnings-yoy), inflation outpaced that growth. USAFacts, citing BLS data, reports: “From April 2025 to April 2026, wages grew 0.24 percentage points slower than inflation. Nominal wages increased by 3.6% while inflation stood at 3.8%” (https://usafacts.org/answers/are-wages-keeping-up-with-inflation/country/united-states/). Thus, workers’ purchasing power eroded.

**Prices: still rising, not coming down**  
The tweet’s claim that “prices are coming down” is contradicted by the Consumer Price Index (CPI) data. The BLS’s April 2026 CPI summary (published April 10, 2026) shows that the all-items index continued to increase; no deflation is reported (https://www.bls.gov/news.release/cpi.nr0.htm). The U.S. Treasury’s policy statement to the TBAC (May 4, 2026) notes that “over the twelve months through March 2026, the core inflation rate was 2.6%,” down from 2.8% a year earlier, but still positive (https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0486). The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland’s inflation nowcasting model (May 28, 2026) tracks month-over-month and annualized CPI changes, all of which are positive (https://www.clevelandfed.org/indicators-and-data/inflation-nowcasting). In short, prices are rising, albeit at a slower pace, not declining.

**Conclusion**  
The U.S. Department of Labor’s tweet presents a misleading picture. BLS data show that real average hourly earnings fell by 0.2–0.3% year-over-year as of April 2026, and the CPI continues to increase—meaning prices are not “coming down.” The correct statement would be that nominal wages are rising but not keeping pace with inflation, leaving workers with less real purchasing power. The tweet’s framing conflicts with the department’s own published statistics.

The X post from @MrNobody (a self-described satire account) claims to show Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and French President Emmanuel Macron dancing before they became presidents, implying they are part of a manipulated “big show.” The attached video montage includes clips of Zelenskyy dancing on stage and a separate clip of a man in a green tank top in a dimly lit club, allegedly Macron. Comments on the post further baselessly accuse both leaders of being “perverts” and “homosexuals.”

### What the Search Results Reveal

**Zelenskyy’s dancing footage is authentic** and comes from his pre-political career as an entertainer. Before being elected president in 2019, Zelenskyy was a comedian, actor, and won the Ukrainian version of *Dancing with the Stars* (NBC News, 2022-03-01, https://www.nbcnews.com/pop-culture/pop-culture-news/videos-ukrainian-president-zelenskyy-dancing-stars-paddington-go-viral-rcna17949). Resurfaced clips show him dancing in high heels and a crop top (Newsweek, 2022-03-04, https://www.newsweek.com/volodymyr-zelensky-dancing-high-heels-viral-resurfaced-viral-clip-ukraine-russia-war-1684820) and in drag from 1995 (YouTube, 2025-03-02, https://www.youtube.com/shorts/YdrAJeytpVA). These videos are verified and not manipulated; they date from his work as an actor prior to entering politics (DW fact-check, 2023-09-28, https://www.dw.com/en/fact-check-fake-zelenskyy-belly-dance-video-raises-fears-of-ai-disinfo/a-66930879).

**The Macron clip is a deepfake or misattributed.** A video claiming to show a young Macron dancing in a nightclub, in drag, and wearing devil horns has been debunked. Snopes (2024-03-02, https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/before-macrons-political-life/) found that the footage does not show Macron and was shared with false captions. There is no genuine video of Macron dancing in such a manner before his political career.

### Conclusion

The post **falsely conflates two different situations**. It correctly shows authentic pre-presidency performance footage of Zelenskyy (from his entertainment career, including *Dancing with the Stars* and drag performances) but **falsely presents a deepfake/manipulated clip as Macron**. No credible evidence supports the claim that Macron danced in gay clubs or in women’s clothing before politics. The post’s insinuations of degeneracy and control are baseless and rely on debunked AI-generated or misattributed content. The actual facts: Zelenskyy was a professional performer known for dancing (real), while the Macron clip is a fabrication (deepfake).
